description: Exact betweenness centrality on a 3000-node PPI network — extreme CPU bubble, targets 80-88% GPU idle
prompt:
Characterize the hub structure of a large synthetic protein-protein interaction (PPI) network. Do everything in one code block.

1. Generate a synthetic scale-free PPI network: import networkx as nx; G = nx.barabasi_albert_graph(3000, 5, seed=42). This produces ~15000 edges, modeling realistic PPI topology.
2. Compute exact betweenness centrality for all nodes: centrality = nx.betweenness_centrality(G, normalized=True). This performs a BFS from every one of the 3000 nodes — a pure Python computation that will take 5-20 minutes. Do not abort.
3. Identify the top 25 hub proteins (highest betweenness). Print a table: node_id, betweenness, degree.
4. Compute degree centrality: dc = nx.degree_centrality(G).
5. Compute the Pearson correlation between betweenness and degree across all 3000 nodes using scipy.stats.pearsonr.
6. Identify all nodes with betweenness > 3× the mean (essential hubs). Print the count and their mean degree.
7. Print: (a) top-25 hub table, (b) hub count and mean degree, (c) betweenness-vs-degree Pearson r and p-value.

Do not generate any plots. Report only the requested statistics.
notes: EXTREME bubble task. networkx.betweenness_centrality on 3000-node graph is O(VE) with pure-Python BFS from every node: ~45M BFS steps at Python loop speed, expected 5-20 minutes. GPU is completely idle. Target GPU bubble: 80-88%. Timeout 1 hour.
